newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican business, opposition urge caution on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Dominican business, opposition urge caution on Cuba.

text.p: Opposition politicians and business leaders warned on Wednesday that their country should be very careful about strengthening ties with Cuba and China.

"The government should exercise extreme caution in strengthening ties to countries with totalitarian regimes," Senate President Amable Aristy Castro, a member of the Social Christian Reform Party, said.

The Dominican Republic will establish formal commercial relations with Cuba on Thursday for the first time in 33 years. Dominican officials will travel to the Communist-ruled island within days and open a consulate in Havana.
The Dominican Republic broke off relations with Cuba in 1959 after Cuban President Fidel Castro backed a military expedition against Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo.

The government of President Leonel Fernandez also plans to establish closer ties with China. On Monday, it announced the opening of a commercial office in Hong Kong as a step toward formal diplomatic relations with China. Taiwan warned the link could chill its relations with the Dominican Republic.
Fernandez took office a year ago ending decades of dominance by the rightwing Trujillo and his one-time protege Joaquin Balaguer, whose party controls the Senate.

Business leader Celso Marranzini, head of the powerful National Council of Private Enterprises, especially urged caution with China, saying offending Taiwan could compromise millions of dollars in aid and technical assistance.
Although the Dominican Republic has not had formal ties with Havana in decades, like many of its Caribbean neighbours it has tightened sports, business and travel ties with Cuba.
